payoutsOnboard.title: Payouts onboarding
payoutsOnboard.intro: Connect a Stripe account to receive payouts from your sales on Cobuntu. Stripe handles the money movement, identity verification, and bank transfers. We only see whether your account is ready to receive payouts.
payoutsOnboard.howBullet1: Payouts run daily. Eligible sales transfer to your Stripe account once they clear the refund window.
payoutsOnboard.howBullet2: Cobuntu doesn't take a cut from your member sales directly: communities take their commission, Stripe takes its processing fee, and the rest is yours.
payoutsOnboard.howBullet3: If a buyer is refunded, the refund-side Stripe fee is deducted from your next payout.
payoutsOnboard.notConnectedDesc: Stripe handles all payment processing and identity verification. The onboarding typically takes about five minutes: you'll need your ID and your bank account details.
payoutsOnboard.onboardingDesc: Stripe still needs more information before they can release payouts. Resuming onboarding drops you back into the exact step Stripe is asking for.
payoutsOnboard.readyDesc: Stripe will receive your payouts on the next daily sweep. You can review balances and history in your Stripe dashboard.
payoutsOnboard.disconnectSummary: Need to disconnect this Stripe account?
payoutsOnboard.disconnectDesc: Disconnecting pauses future payouts until you connect a new account. Any sales already eligible for payout will stay eligible: they'll just wait for a destination.

howReferralsWorkContent.pillarShareBody: When your community runs a referral program, you get a personal link. It can also assign you a dedicated one with its own rate. Anyone who joins and pays through it is credited to you.
howReferralsWorkContent.pillarEarnBody: The commission recurs. You earn on the first payment and on each renewal, for the duration the community sets: a fixed number of payments, or the membership's lifetime.
howReferralsWorkContent.pillarPayBody: Commissions are batched by currency and paid to your Stripe account on the platform's payout schedule. Every payout comes with a remittance statement.
howReferralsWorkContent.pillarZeroBody: Your commission comes out of the community's share, after Cobuntu's platform fee. Cobuntu takes no part of your referral commission.
howReferralsWorkContent.moneySubhead: On a €100 monthly membership, with an 8% referral rate:
howReferralsWorkContent.earnParagraph: You earn that €8 every month the member keeps paying, for the program's duration. Both fees come out of the amount actually paid, so a discount or coupon scales them down. Every community sets its own rate and duration, so your numbers may differ.
howReferralsWorkContent.detailConnectBody: You need a Stripe account that can receive payouts. Your link stays inactive until you connect one. If your payout ability lapses, commissions pause and resume automatically once you can be paid again. Cobuntu never holds them in the meantime.
howReferralsWorkContent.detailRefundBody: A commission is held through the member's refund window and only becomes payable after it passes. If their payment is refunded or charged back before you are paid it is cancelled; if it happens after, it is reversed.
howReferralsWorkContent.detailPrivateBody: Your tracker shows how many people you referred, what you have earned, and when your next commission is expected. It never reveals who they are.
howReferralsWorkContent.detailTaxBody: You are responsible for any tax due on the commissions you earn. Each payout comes with a remittance statement to help you account for it.
howReferralsWorkContent.detailSelfBody: You cannot earn a commission on your own membership. The program rewards you for bringing in other people.

sellingOnCobuntu.metaDescription: How selling works on Cobuntu: what you get, what the community gets, how approval works.
sellingOnCobuntu.intro: You can list products and host events in any Cobuntu community that allows member sellers. Here's how it works.
sellingOnCobuntu.ownBody: Every product or event you list is yours. Your name is on it, your payouts go to your own Stripe account, and you set the price. Communities act as the channel - they help you reach members - but they never take ownership of your work.
sellingOnCobuntu.brokersBody: When you list in a community, the community takes a commission on each sale. The rate depends on the community's pricing model:
sellingOnCobuntu.flatCommission: Flat commission - every member uses the same rate set by community leaders, indexed by what you're selling (product or event).
sellingOnCobuntu.dynamicCommission: Dynamic commission - each listing is negotiated individually with community leaders before going live.
sellingOnCobuntu.brokersRates: The exact rates for this community are on <guide>{community}'s selling guide</guide>.
sellingOnCobuntu.zeroFeeBody: Cobuntu earns from the community's commission, not from your revenue. You receive the full sale price minus the community's commission and standard Stripe processing fees. There's no separate Cobuntu fee on top.
sellingOnCobuntu.approvalBody1: Depending on the community's policy, your listing either goes live the moment you submit it, or it enters a review queue first. When review is required, community leaders see your submission, can ask questions in a dedicated chat, and approve or decline.
sellingOnCobuntu.approvalBody2: Communities using the dynamic commission model always review every listing - the review IS the negotiation.
sellingOnCobuntu.stripeTitle: Paid listings need a connected Stripe account
sellingOnCobuntu.stripeBody: To accept money you need to connect your own Stripe account - Cobuntu doesn't hold funds on your behalf. Free listings work without one. You'll be prompted to connect Stripe the first time you try to set a price.
sellingOnCobuntu.restrictionBody: Members can't scope listings to specific membership tiers ("only Gold members can buy this"). Tier-gating is reserved for community-owned listings, so leaders can offer tier-exclusive perks without member sellers being able to claim the same lever.
sellingOnCobuntu.ctaFootnote: The link is enabled only if {community} has the matching member-listing toggle on. See <guide>{community}'s selling guide</guide> for what's currently allowed here.

buyerRights.aKeeps: Nothing that reaches you can be taken back. Your purchase saves its own copy of the listing and its files at the moment you buy, so editing the listing, or removing it entirely, does not touch what you already paid for. It stays in your library.

buyerRights.refundProduct: A full refund, for any reason, within 14 days of buying. After that the seller has been paid and a refund is theirs to agree to.
buyerRights.refundProductPhysical: You have 14 days from the day it arrives to change your mind and start a return. You pay the postage to send it back, and the money returns once the seller confirms it reached them. If they say nothing for 14 days after you post it, we refund you anyway.
buyerRights.refundEvent: A full refund, for any reason, until the event ends. Some hosts turn off self-service refunds, in which case the button asks you to contact them instead.
buyerRights.refundEventTbd: This event has no confirmed date yet, so you have a full refund for 30 days from purchase.
buyerRights.aNeverShips: The seller has about five working days to hand the parcel over. If they do not, the order cancels itself and you are refunded in full, without you having to chase it.
buyerRights.qEventCancelled: If the host cancels the event
buyerRights.aEventCancelled: Cancelling, deleting or unpublishing an event refunds every ticket in full. That happens on its own, the moment the host does it, so there is nothing for you to claim and nobody to ask.
buyerRights.qApproval: If the seller has to approve you first
buyerRights.aApproval: Your payment is held, not taken. Nothing reaches the seller until they approve, and you are not charged a platform fee on a request that is turned down. If they never answer, the request is cancelled after 14 days and you get everything back.
buyerRights.qApprovalEvent: If the host has to approve you first
buyerRights.aApprovalEvent: Your payment is held, not taken. Nothing reaches the host until they approve you, and you are not charged a platform fee on a request that is turned down. If they never answer, the request is cancelled and refunded in full after 14 days, or within a few days of the event ending, whichever comes first.
buyerRights.aAfterRefund: Access ends with the money. A refunded purchase leaves your library and its files stop downloading, which is what keeps a refund from being a free copy.
buyerRights.aAfterRefundPhysical: The item goes back first, then the money moves. That order is deliberate: it is what stops a seller being left with neither the item nor the payment.
buyerRights.aAfterRefundEvent: Your place is released. The registration is cancelled and the seat returns to the event for someone else, so a refund is never a ticket you keep.
buyerRights.aProblem: Message the seller first, since most things are quicker to fix directly. If that does not work, contact Cobuntu and we will look at the payment ourselves.
buyerRights.aProblemEvent: Message the host first, since most things are quicker to fix directly. If that does not work, contact Cobuntu and we will look at the payment ourselves.
